items.title: City Council Approves Year-Long Hold on New Data Centre Approvals in Mississauga
items.summary: City council has approved a motion directing staff to prepare an Interim Control By-law that would block approval of new digital infrastructure projects, including data centres, for up to one year, the City of Mississauga says. The measure targets a category of development that has drawn increasing attention as demand for these facilities grows. Alongside the temporary hold, staff have also been directed to carry out a full review of this emerging sector. That review will look at whether existing planning tools, including the Official Plan and the Zoning By-law, need to be updated to properly address large-scale digital infrastructure. City officials point to a broader driver behind the move: rising use of digital services across Canada is fueling demand for bigger, more powerful data centres. The city's approach pairs an immediate, time-limited restriction with a longer study, giving staff room to work out updated rules before more such projects come forward for approval.

items.title: Emancipation Day Marked in Mississauga With Flag-Raising and a Call to Learn Local Black History
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, Emancipation Day falls on August 1 each year and is set aside for reflection, education and celebration of the strength and resilience of people of African descent, as well as the ongoing fight against racism and discrimination. The city is marking the occasion with a Pan-African flag-raising ceremony, part of its effort to recognize the day publicly. Residents are being encouraged to take part in more than just the ceremony itself. The city is also pointing people toward the local library's curated reading list, which highlights the contributions and achievements of Black individuals in Canada. Together, the events are meant to give the community a chance to engage with the history and significance behind Emancipation Day, not just observe it in passing.

items.title: Rising Gas Prices Are Squeezing Household Budgets Already Stretched Thin, City Says
items.summary: Surging gas prices are adding real financial strain to Mississauga households, the City of Mississauga says, with transportation now the third-largest household expense for Canadians after shelter and food. That ranking comes from Statistics Canada's most recent Survey of Household Spending, conducted in 2023. The pressure is landing on families that already have little room to absorb it. New data from United Way Centraide Canada, released in June 2026, found that 46 per cent of people in Canada could cover their basic living expenses for only one month or less if their income stopped. Against that backdrop, the city says, rising and unpredictable gas prices are piling even more stress onto budgets that were already stretched before prices climbed further.
